arms.label: 1D CNNs on one-dimensional DNA token sequences

evidence.quote: This section presents a controlled accuracy-efficiency comparison between (i) 1D CNNs that operate on DNA as a onedimensional token sequence and (ii) 2D CNNs that operate on our DNA document representation, where each DNA sequence is rendered into n pages of 640 × 640 images (with n determined by sequence length).
On accuracy, lightweight 2D models such as TinyNet-E achieve the best average AUROC (0.786), exceeding all 1D CNN variants in our comparison (CNN1D-small/base/large/xl).

representation_comparisons.numbers_stated: TinyNet-E: AUROC 0.786, epoch time 66.9 s, throughput 33.7 samples/s; SimpleCNN: AUROC 0.528; 1D CNN variants: AUROC 0.553-0.649
representation_comparisons.result_summary: The 2D rendered-document representation achieved the best accuracy-efficiency trade-off in this comparison.

evidence.quote: Specifically, the same genomic input is represented either as a 1D sequence or as a 2D image document. For the 2D setting, the input is rendered as a 336 × 336 genomic image document. Both representations are tokenized and reduced to the same number of tokens, i.e., 10,000 tokens, and then processed by the same Transformer backbone under the same training and evaluation pipeline.
The 2D image-document representation achieves 0.626 AUROC, compared with 0.558 AUROC for the 1D sequence representation.

representation_comparisons.numbers_stated: 10,000 tokens for both; 2D image document 0.626 AUROC; 1D sequence 0.558 AUROC; 12.20% relative improvement
representation_comparisons.result_summary: Under matched token count and a shared Transformer backbone, the 2D image-document representation performed better.

evidence.quote: Among these 1D baselines, the RNN model performs the best, achieving an average AUROC of 0.6575. The linear-attention (LinearAttn) and sparse-attention (SparseAttn) baselines achieve 0.6279 and 0.6163 AUROC, respectively. However, all of them remain substantially below the 2D baselines, including TinyNet-E and OpticalDNA.

representation_comparisons.result_summary: Stronger 1D sequence architectures remained below the 2D document-style models.

evidence.quote: Table 7 shows that as the resolution increases from 512 to 1280, the number of visual tokens per page rises from 64 to 400 and the compression ratio increases from 19.0 to 21.2, while the average AUROC remains nearly unchanged (0.849-0.852).

representation_comparisons.numbers_stated: Average AUROC 0.849-0.852; compression ratio 19.0-21.2; 64-400 visual tokens per page
representation_comparisons.result_summary: Increasing visual resolution and token count changed compression substantially while AUROC remained nearly unchanged.

evidence.quote: Reducing the token budget from 100 to 50 or 20 retained tokens yields only mild performance changes, with average AUROC remaining 0.842-0.846 compared with 0.852 under the original 100-token setting. Performance degrades more noticeably under severe bottlenecks of 10 tokens or fewer, and drops to 0.776 when the entire sequence is compressed into a single token.

representation_comparisons.result_summary: The original 100-token representation was strongest; moderate compression caused mild changes and severe compression caused clear degradation.

evidence.quote: Continuous layouts that preserve horizontal sequence continuity tend to perform better than rigid fixed-window layouts.

fixed-window layouts with 32, 48, or 64 bp per line obtain 0.758-0.774 AUROC (fixed win 32, fixed win 48, fixed win 64). Similarly, a fixed-block layout with 64 bp windows and one gap line reaches 0.777 AUROC (fixed block 64 gap1).

representation_comparisons.numbers_stated: Default continuous layout 0.813 AUROC; fixed-window/fixed-block 0.758-0.777; wide dense continuous 0.858
representation_comparisons.result_summary: Layouts preserving local sequence continuity outperformed rigid partitioning layouts.

evidence.quote: OpticalDNA shows graceful degradation under downsampling: performance remains strong at moderate resolutions, with 256 × 256 yielding 0.812 AUROC, nearly matching the original 640 × 640 result of 0.813, and 320 × 320 achieving 0.828 AUROC.

representation_comparisons.result_summary: Moderate downsampling preserved performance, while extreme downsampling reduced AUROC.

evidence.quote: Starting-position shifts yield cosine similarities between 0.904 and 0.985, with an average of 0.937. Resolution changes also preserve strong consistency, with similarities ranging from 0.776 to 0.984 and an average of 0.899. General layout perturbations achieve an average similarity of 0.879.
The main degradation occurs only under extreme layout changes, such as comparing dense continuous rendering with fixed-window rendering, where the similarity can drop to 0.564.

representation_comparisons.metric: pairwise cosine similarity of extracted representations
representation_comparisons.numbers_stated: Starting-position average 0.937; resolution average 0.899; general layout average 0.879; extreme fixed-window comparison as low as 0.564
representation_comparisons.result_summary: Representations were highly consistent under common perturbations, with larger changes under extreme layout changes.
representation_comparisons.task: Representation consistency across rendered DNA formats

evidence.quote: we render 1D sequences into structured 2D layouts, converting discontinuous long-range dependencies into spatial structure amenable to region-aware inductive biases

representation_rationale.summary: The 2D document layout is intended to make sparse, discontinuous genomic dependencies spatially accessible.

evidence.quote: base-level content is mapped into compact, reconstructible vision tokens (Fig. 1d), substantially reducing the effective token count compared with base or k -mer tokenization while preserving fine-grained information.

representation_rationale.summary: The representation reduces effective token count while preserving reconstructible nucleotide information.

evidence.quote: By converting a long sequence into a coordinate-indexed document, OpticalDNA enables region-level access patterns similar to document understanding and OCR: the model can process local visual regions, aggregate page-level information, and perform prompt-conditioned operations such as reading, grounding, retrieval, and completion.

representation_rationale.summary: The document interface supports region-level access, grounding, retrieval, completion, and page-level aggregation.

evidence.quote: Existing genomic foundation models inherit inductive biases from natural language modeling, assuming dense semantics under exhaustive token-by-token reading
As a result, sequential reading is structurally wasteful: most computation is spent scanning background rather than modeling sparse functional regions

representation_rationale.summary: The authors criticize sequential token processing for allocating computation to low-information genomic background.

evidence.quote: Importantly, this rendering is intentionally simple and does not introduce explicit biological priors. It does not encode genomic landmarks, strand-aware structure, chromatin contacts, regulatory annotations, or biologically grounded spatial layouts.

representation_rationale.summary: The visual rendering is computational rather than biologically grounded and omits explicit biological priors.

evidence.quote: very low resolutions can degrade performance by removing fine-grained nucleotide-level visual details.
extreme perturbations that disrupt local sequence continuity can change the learned representation and moderately reduce downstream performance.

representation_rationale.summary: Fine-grained visual detail and preservation of local sequence continuity remain important limitations of the representation.
